prompt: Why does the C=O of a cyclopentanone (five-membered ring ketone) appear at ~1745 cm⁻¹, HIGHER than acetone (1715)?

options.label: Ring strain forces smaller internal angles at the carbonyl C, increasing s-character of the C=O bond and raising its force constant.

explanation: Smaller rings compress the C–C=O angle; the C must use more p-character for the ring σ bonds and MORE s-character for the C=O π/σ system → stiffer C=O → higher frequency. The trend: cyclohexanone 1715 ≈ acetone, cyclopentanone 1745, cyclobutanone 1780, cyclopropanone 1815.
